ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Automobile trunk lids generally are equipped with retractable hydraulic rods, as shown in Figure 3A; its schematic diagram is as shown in Figure 3B. The upper end of the retractable hydraulic rod is fixed at point A on the rear lid, the lower end is fixed at point O' inside the trunk, and B is also a point on the rear lid. The rear lid can rotate around the fixed hinge passing through point O. In the process of closing the trunk lid, what is the relationship between the magnitudes of the angular velocities of point A and point B rotating relative to point O?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The magnitudes of the angular velocities of point A and point B rotating relative to point O are equal
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is a real-object picture of an automobile trunk lid opened; it can be seen that the rear lid is supported by support rods on both sides. In the schematic diagram on the right, the thick inclined rod represents the rear lid; it rotates around the fixed hinge O at the lower right end; points A and B are both marked on this thick inclined rod, namely the rear lid; the lower end of the retractable hydraulic rod is connected to point O' inside the car body, and the upper end is connected to point A on the rear lid; the curved arrow beside it indicates that when closing the lid, the rear lid rotates around O. Reasoning: The stem states that the rear lid can rotate around the fixed hinge passing through point O, and A and B are both points on the rear lid. Therefore, when closing the trunk lid, point A and point B, together with the same rigid body rear lid, make fixed-axis rotation around the same fixed point O. When a rigid body makes fixed-axis rotation, the angular velocities of all points on the rigid body are the same; the distances from different points to O may be different, so the linear velocities may be different, but the magnitudes of the angular velocities of rotation relative to O are equal.
